summary: Backend-only testing of Smart AI Face Recognition. All 30 pytest tests passed on 1st clean run: auth (login/logout/me + invalid creds), engine health (buffalo_l ready), users CRUD, real InsightFace enrollment with a genuine portrait (obama.jpg, 512-d ArcFace embedding saved), single-frame /api/recognize returns status=known with similarity >= 0.42 for enrolled user, /api/recognize/multi majority-voting returns known + logs attendance + attendance_logged field present, noise images correctly rejected on enroll and produce status=no_face on recognize, attendance/recognition-history/unknowns/dashboard-stats endpoints return expected shapes, and 9 protected endpoints correctly return 401 without a Bearer token while /api/, /api/health/engine, /api/auth/login and /api/auth/logout are public.

minor.issue: Referenced in /app/memory/test_credentials.md but not implemented in server.py — either implement it or remove from the docs.

backend/.env has CORS_ORIGINS="*" while cookies are set with SameSite=none Secure and CORSMiddleware uses allow_credentials=True. Browsers reject Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with credentials; frontend cookie auth will silently fail cross-origin. Set CORS_ORIGINS to explicit origin(s) (e.g. the REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL host).
No brute-force lockout / rate limiting implemented (playbook expects lockout after 5 failed attempts). Not blocking MVP but worth adding.
Returns 200 for creation instead of the more conventional 201 Created (not blocking).

action_items: Consider setting CORS_ORIGINS in backend/.env to the explicit frontend origin instead of '*' so httpOnly cookie auth works cross-origin (browsers block '*' when allow_credentials=True).
Either implement POST /api/auth/register (referenced in /app/memory/test_credentials.md) or remove it from the credentials doc.
Optional: add login rate-limiting/lockout for brute-force protection.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup')/'shutdown' hooks — migrate to lifespan handlers.
CORS + cookies mismatch (allow_credentials=True with allow_origins=['*']) is a real cross-origin auth risk in production; fine for same-origin ingress but should be tightened.

No embedding de-duplication in enrollment: sending the same image N times stores N nearly-identical vectors and inflates the gallery. Consider a similarity threshold check against existing embeddings for the same user_id before insert.

face_engine.decode_base64_image / analyze / quality_check are synchronous and CPU-heavy; they run inside FastAPI request handlers on the event loop and can block other requests. Wrap in run_in_executor / asyncio.to_thread for better concurrency.
engine.status() is read without holding self._lock (minor race with _load thread).
quality_check uses fixed pixel thresholds (min 60x60, blur<40, brightness 35..235). Values look sensible but not configurable via env.
recognize_multi has ratio threshold 0.4 that means with 3 frames a single winning vote passes majority — arguably too permissive; consider majority (>0.5) with a minimum-frames guard.
seed_data_creation: Tests create a transient TEST_Obama user (unique employee_id TEST_EMP_001) with 4 real InsightFace embeddings from /app/test_fixtures/portrait.jpg, then delete it in fixture teardown. A TestUserLifecycle._cleanup_prior fixture also purges any stale TEST_* users from previous runs so the gallery stays deterministic across retries.
context_for_next_testing_agent: conftest.py exposes base_url, api_client, authed_client, portrait_b64 (real single-face obama.jpg from /app/test_fixtures), and noise_b64 (random-noise image). All interdependent tests (create → enroll → recognize → attendance/history) live inside TestUserLifecycle so xdist loadscope keeps them on one worker (loadscope groups by CLASS for methods, not by module). If you split them across classes you'll get two TEST_Obama users enrolled with the same portrait and recognize will match the wrong id. Face engine reports ready=true instantly on this pod. FACE_MATCH_THRESHOLD=0.42; obama.jpg self-similarity is well above threshold.
rca_of_previous_run: Initial run failed 3 tests because tests were split into TestEnrollment / TestRecognizeSingle / TestRecognizeMulti / TestListEndpoints. pytest-xdist --dist loadscope groups by test class (not module) for methods, so the module-scoped `created_user_id` fixture was instantiated on both workers, creating two TEST_Obama users with identical portrait embeddings. Multi-frame recognition then matched the other worker's user_id. Fix: consolidated all interdependent methods into one TestUserLifecycle class with a class-scoped user_id fixture — now runs on exactly one worker with a single canonical user id. No backend change required.
